newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur fuel falls hard, market seen long.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur fuel falls hard, market seen long.

text.p: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were sharply lower on Monday, despite marginally firmer crude oil, following a very discounted trade on Friday, traders said.
January swaps were flat to February after having slipped by $3-$4 a tonne to talk at around $121 fob NWE.
Dealers said a refiner sold a distressed U.K.-origin cargo to another refiner on Friday but the price, which was not confirmed, was said to have been as low as $120 cif NWE -- well below the market.

At least three other low sulphur pieces are thought available for early January. Italian demand for January was hard to assess, with the region's main buyer still absent because of a national holiday.
Low sulphur straight-run fuel was little changed from Friday, when deals were heard done at near to $144 cif NWE for an Irish piece, and at $137 fob NWE for a piece out of ARA.
High sulphur barges traded at $115 and $115.50 fob ARA.
Because of poor bunker demand, barges failed to respond positively to news that Esso Rotterdam had restarted its flexi-coking unit at the weekend.
Cargoes were seen stable. An end user saw two availabilities so far for early to mid January -- one from Scandinavia and the other from the U.K. He said offers were at $118 cif NWE.
